items.title: Major volcanic eruptions inject ash into the stratosphere
items.claim: How high can a large eruption column reach?

options.text: Up to 5 km — high but contained in the troposphere
Plinian eruptions can exceed 30-40 km, well into the stratosphere — Mount Pinatubo (1991) reached around 35 km
Only the visible smoke is observable
No eruption has reached the stratosphere in recorded history

items.reveal:
Plinian eruptions (named after Pliny the Younger's description of Vesuvius in 79 CE) drive ash and sulphate aerosols into the stratosphere, where they can spread globally and remain for years. Pinatubo (June 1991) cooled global temperatures by around 0.5°C for 18 months.

Tambora (1815, VEI 7) caused the 'Year Without a Summer' (1816) — crop failures across Europe and North America, snow in June. Krakatoa (1883, VEI 6) produced spectacular sunsets globally. Toba (around 74,000 years ago, VEI 8) may have caused a population bottleneck in early humans.
items.why: Volcanic forcing is one of the strongest natural climate drivers on year-to-decade scales. Climate models calibrate against these events because the signal is large and well-dated.

items.title: HDI combines health, education and income
items.claim: Why does the UN use HDI as well as GDP?

options.text: GDP is sufficient for all purposes

The Human Development Index (1990, devised by Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen) combines life expectancy, education (mean and expected years of schooling) and GNI per capita — capturing health and education outcomes that GDP misses

items.reveal:
The HDI uses three components — life expectancy, education, GNI per capita (PPP) — each normalised between 0 and 1, combined as a geometric mean (since 2010).

Top HDI rankings (2022): Switzerland, Norway, Iceland. UK 15th, US 21st. Bottom: Niger, South Sudan, Somalia. The Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) drops the US further than the UK because of US within-country inequality.

The UN now also tracks the Gender Inequality Index (GII), the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) and the SDG indicators. Critics: the HDI averages three different things and can obscure trade-offs.
items.why: What gets measured shapes priorities. A country that has converted wealth into health and education is a meaningfully different policy success than one with high GDP and poor outcomes.

items.title: The jet stream sits around 10 km up at the tropopause

options.text: A narrow band of fast westerly winds (typically 100-300 km/h) at around 9-12 km altitude, near the tropopause, driven by temperature contrasts between polar and tropical air masses
An ocean current in the Pacific
A jet of supersonic air over deserts

items.reveal:
The polar jet (which shapes UK weather) and the subtropical jet are the major Northern Hemisphere features. They meander in Rossby waves; the shape of those waves controls where storm tracks lie.

Jet streams were discovered by Japanese balloon-bombing campaigns of WWII and by US B-29 crews over the Pacific (1944) — flying west into apparently impossible headwinds. Carl-Gustaf Rossby's work in the 1930s-40s framed them theoretically.

Arctic amplification reduces the temperature contrast that drives the polar jet, possibly causing it to meander more — linked to more persistent weather extremes (heat domes, stuck storm tracks).
items.why: Surface weather has upper-atmosphere causes. Understanding why summer 2022 had heat domes or why winter 2013-14 had stuck Atlantic storm tracks requires looking at jet stream geometry.
